messages:
Marta (Design): Dropped a new export-preview comp — shows a live preview of column/field order before you hit Export. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/preview/export-ordering

Marta (Design): Main questions: 1) default ordering (corr_id first?) 2) should users be able to drag to reorder columns in the modal preview? 3) keyboard + SR interactions for reordering.

Ryan (Design): Love drag-to-reorder in the preview. Visual affordance: small drag handle on the left of each column chip, with a live reorder animation. On small screens collapse to a simple list.

Sam (Eng): Reordering is fine. Implementation note: reorder only in the client UI, send the final array to the export endpoint as export_columns=["corr_id","timestamp","service",...]. We'll persist user defaults per-org.

Nina (A11y): Important: drag-and-drop must have a keyboard-accessible alternative. Provide a keyboard reorder mode: focus a chip, press Space to pick it up, arrow keys to move, Space to drop. Announce moves via aria-live polite: "Correlation ID moved to position 1". Also ensure each chip has a clear aria-label like "Column: Correlation ID, position 2 of 6".

Alex (Product): Default ordering: corr_id first for request exports, yes. But for full-trace exports customers sometimes prefer timestamp first. Proposal: default corr_id first for 'Requests' scope and timestamp first for 'Trace' scope; add a small dropdown in the modal: 'Suggested order: Requests / Traces'.

Priya (Support): We should include copy that clarifies what each column contains. Tooltip under each chip: short description + whether it contains potentially sensitive info. Eg: "Correlation ID — unique request identifier (may reveal internal routing)". Customers will ask about removing/masking.

Sam (Eng): For masking, support the export flag mask_sensitive=true which will redact corr_ids to a shortened format. Also for analytics: we'll log export event with columns chosen for product telemetry. Keep that opt-out for privacy-conscious orgs.

Marta (Design): UX for the preview: show a tiny table sample below the chips with 3 rows so users can immediately see the effect of reordering and masking. For accessibility ensure the sample table is keyboard-navigable and that SRs can read header order.

Nina (A11y): For the sample table, add aria-describedby pointing to a concise description: "Preview: columns in current order. Use drag handles or press Space on a column to enter reorder mode." When a column order changes, announce: "Preview updated: Correlation ID is now first column." Don't use aria-live for large contents. Keep announcements short.

Ryan (Design): Small microcopy: button label 'Customize export' and inside modal title 'Export preview & order'. For reordering affordance use a handle icon and subtle shadow when dragging.

Alex (Product): Add a persistence layer: remember last custom order per-user and per-org default. Also include a 'Reset to suggested order' link. Modal copy: helper line: "Default suggestions are optimized for cross-system debugging."

Priya (Support): Add support guidance: how to mask corr_ids before sharing externally and how to remove columns. I'll draft a short FAQ blurb.

Sam (Eng): JSON payload example we'll accept: {"trace_id":"t-1","export_columns":["corr_id","timestamp","service","message"],"mask_sensitive":true}. We'll also support export_scope: "related" | "full".

Marta (Design): Keyboard shortcuts idea: when modal open, press 'R' to toggle reorder mode, arrow keys move focused chip, Enter confirms. Sound OK?

Nina (A11y): That's okay if we surface it in the modal header and ensure no conflicts. Make sure Escape cancels reorder mode and returns focus. Also document the exact SR strings. I'll add short examples: aria-labels and live announcements.

Ryan (Design): One more: inline preview when toggling 'Export annotations' — show small annotation pill column (icon) that expands to show text in the sample rows. Keep it collapsed by default.

Sam (Eng): We'll add export_annotations flag and include_annotations_visibility to determine which annotations are exported. Backend will accept columns like "annotation_text" and/or "annotation_meta.author" too.

Marta (Design): Action items: Ryan update Figma with drag-handle and sample table; Sam prototype modal UI + API payload; Nina write the a11y reorder spec and announcement strings; Alex finalize product copy for defaults and persistence; Priya draft support FAQ. CLI-bot: add reminder to tag PRs.

CLI-bot: integration reminder scheduled for 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC 1: tag PRs with #export-preview.

Marta (Design): Thanks all. If no objections I'll ship the label 'Customize export' and the corr_id-first suggested order for request exports by EOD. :white_check_mark:
